headline: Highest risk is data leakage: Chatwoot handles customer data while Slim can read/write files and use broad network egress, creating a plausible sensitive-data exposure path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Chatwoot can expose messages and reports, but there is no documented shared channel or direct ingestion path into Slim beyond manual transfer. Slim is an interactive CLI that reads files and executes commands, so prompt-style injection is only plausible if an operator copies Chatwoot content into Slim inputs. The pairwise pathway exists but is not default.
conditions: IF an operator pastes Chatwoot conversation text into Slim's CLI prompt, then instruction-like content can influence Slim.
IF Chatwoot exports messages into a file that Slim later parses as commands or config, then injection becomes possible.
mitigations: Use copy/paste only for sanitized excerpts.
Keep Chatwoot exports in a separate folder from Slim inputs.
Add a one-line prefix note that pasted text is untrusted.
Review any pasted command blocks before execution.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Chatwoot touches customer data, contact profiles, interaction history, orders, and messages, while Slim reads files and handles registry credentials and filesystem artifacts. Because Slim has broad network egress and file access, a shared workspace or copied artifacts could expose sensitive Chatwoot data to Slim's processing and outbound connections. This is plausible in default operator workflows, though not proven by direct integration.
conditions: IF Chatwoot exports customer records into files that Slim reads, then those records can be exposed in Slim's session.
IF Slim is run in a workspace containing Chatwoot exports or logs, then sensitive data may be transmitted outward.
mitigations: Keep Chatwoot exports out of Slim's working directory.
Redact customer identifiers before any handoff.
Disable outbound network access during analysis when feasible.
Use a dedicated throwaway directory for Slim runs.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation between the tools.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Chatwoot is a customer-support system with API integrations, while Slim can execute shell commands, read/write files, and contact Docker and registry APIs. Their write surfaces do not obviously overlap on the same mutable resource, but if an operator points both at the same files or registry artifacts, concurrent modification and overwrite conflicts are plausible. Uncertainty remains because no shared locking or orchestrator is documented.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to modify the same exported files, then write conflicts can occur.
IF Chatwoot-generated artifacts are also used as Slim inputs, then one agent may overwrite the other's working state.
mitigations: Separate the tools into different directories.
Avoid concurrent edits to shared exports.
Snapshot files before handing them to Slim.
Use read-only mounts for Chatwoot outputs.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared artifacts.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Chatwoot can produce customer-facing content and reports, and Slim can act on files and command output without an explicit verification layer. If Chatwoot output is treated as authoritative input for Slim workflows, errors or malformed content can cascade into downstream actions. The pair is not documented as a verified pipeline, so the risk is inferred but credible.
conditions: IF Chatwoot output is fed into Slim commands or config without review, then errors can propagate downstream.
IF Slim automation consumes Chatwoot-generated artifacts as authoritative, then malformed data can trigger incorrect actions.
mitigations: Insert a manual review step between tools.
Validate file formats before Slim consumes them.
Use checksums for transferred artifacts.
Limit Slim to read-only inspection of Chatwoot outputs.
requires-engineering: add schema validation to the handoff.

E_compliance.rationale: Chatwoot clearly handles customer data and messages, while Slim handles filesystem artifacts and registry credentials. If customer data or regulated content is exported into Slim's environment, retention and residency controls may diverge from Chatwoot's support workflow. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so the safest classification is a moderate compliance mismatch risk.
conditions: IF regulated customer records are exported from Chatwoot into Slim-managed files, then retention and access controls may diverge.
IF Slim processes data subject to stricter residency or deletion rules, then compliance obligations may be breached.
mitigations: Avoid moving regulated records into Slim.
Strip secrets from any transferred artifacts.
Document retention for shared files.
Delete temporary exports immediately after use.
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies across both tools.
